issue_context.title: Affected rows are incorrect when updating a table with partitions
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->
```sql
drop table if exists t;
create table t (c_int int, c_str varchar(40), primary key (c_int, c_str) ) partition by hash (c_int) partitions 4;
insert into t values (9, 'angry williams'), (10, 'thirsty hugle');
update t set c_int = c_int + 10, c_str = 'adoring stonebraker' where c_int in (10, 9);
```

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

Only 2 rows get affected.

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

```
mysql> update t set c_int = c_int + 10, c_str = 'adoring stonebraker' where c_int in (10, 9);
Query OK, 4 rows affected (0.06 sec)
Rows matched: 2  Changed: 2  Warnings: 0
```
It seems the data is correct after update, only affected-rows in the response is wrong.

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->
master @ 8978773f5e3d43a100550e6babea9904a99e5938
release-4.0 @ 7cac557b024f0aaca6825193477e5e6daea7055b
comments:
Verified against master. To clarify, which result is incorrect:
```sql
mysql> update t set c_int = c_int + 10, c_str = 'adoring stonebraker' where c_int in (10, 9);
Query OK, 4 rows affected (0.02 sec) <------ This line is wrong
Rows matched: 2  Changed: 2  Warnings: 0 <---- This line is fine
```

The affected rows is calculated repeatly [here](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/0448a548751931dac86ddcc557e83187eeb3a395/executor/write.go#L214) in the executor package and [here](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/0448a548751931dac86ddcc557e83187eeb3a395/table/tables/tables.go#L737) in table package.

Despite the fact this is a bug, I have to gently point out that affected rows is not very accurate in TiDB.

For example, in optimistic transaction mode, the affected rows can't be accurate because the changes are cached in the memory, the transaction may conflict and fail to commit later.
Another example is tne unique key existence check, TiDB may presume unique key not exist and delay the check to transaction commit for the sake of performance, so a statement may say it affected XXX rows and later fail.

A user should not rely on the affected row counts to judge the operation success or fail.
IMO, this is **not a critical problem** that we need to fix immediately.
